rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding account of the House and its rites shows that Quraysh violated its sanctity and therefore had no right to remain its occupants.
rows.anchor: it is shown that the Quraysh have totally

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verses imply that Muslims, rather than Quraysh, are the House's true custodians, but they were powerless in Makkah; after migration they formed a community and sought its blessings.
rows.anchor: the real custodians of the House of God are the Muslims and not the Quraysh. However, in Makkah, they were utterly helpless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expelled Muslims could expect Quraysh to deny them pilgrimage; attempting ḥajj or ʿumrah could bring war within the Ḥaram during sacred months, forbidden in both jāhiliyyah custom and Islam.
rows.anchor: within the precincts of the Ḥaram in the sacred months, something regarded to be forbidden both in the jāhiliyyah customs and in Islam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh and its People of the Book allies used the issue to accuse Muslims of violating sacred places; the following verses answer the questions this raised.
rows.anchor: In the following verses, these questions have been answered

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives oppressed Muslims glad tidings that the time has come for them to defend their rights and that He will support them at every step.
rows.anchor: the time has now arrived when Muslims should protect and defend their rights; God will be with them and will help them at every step

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle إِنَّ emphasizes the attributes stated in the verse.
rows.anchor: the word 9 is to emphasize the attributes mentioned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi identifies the Quraysh as the khawwan kafur; khawwan means utterly dishonest, traitorous, and one who breaks promises.
rows.anchor: a person who is utterly dishonest, is a traitor and who does not honour his promise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh broke the promises and commitments on which they received custodianship, dishonoured Abraham's purpose for the House, and forgot the responsibilities he assigned his descendants.
rows.anchor: these people had broken all their promises and commitments on the basis of which they had been granted the custodianship of the House of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafur, paired with khawwan, expresses Quraysh's ingratitude for the favour of the House.
rows.anchor: instead of duly valuing this favour and being grateful to their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh's religious and political leadership over Arabia came from the House, yet they used custodianship dictatorially, took its privileges, neglected duties, and disrespected it.
rows.anchor: the status of religious and political leadership acquired by the Quraysh over all of Arabia was entirely because of the House of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's statement that He never likes such people means that He hates these devious individuals.
rows.anchor: The expression “never likes” in fact means that God hates such devious individuals

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's respite has expired: God will cleanse His House of them and transfer its custody to those who fulfil its duties.
rows.anchor: the time has come that God will cleanse His House from their filth and consign its custodianship to those who will duly discharge their responsibilities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction suppresses an implicit permission: Muslims against whom war is waged are allowed to wage war in response.
rows.anchor: The implication is that those Muslims have been permitted to wage war against whom war is waged

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muslims became a community they were told to be patient despite oppression; individual fighting cannot restrain disorder or establish justice, which is the purpose of war in Islam.
rows.anchor: in the absence of any collectivity, any war waged by individuals cannot curb disorder and create justice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After migration to Madīnah circumstances changed, so Muslims received permission to take up arms in defence.
rows.anchor: Once Muslims migrated to Madīnah, circumstances changed. For this reason, they were allowed to take up arms in defence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the permission concerned the Ḥaram and its boundaries, Muslims needed authorization from God and His messenger before acting there.
rows.anchor: Muslims could not have taken any step regarding the Ḥaram unless they were given permission by God and His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only defensive warfare was permitted at this stage because Muslims could bear no further burden; Islahi directs readers to his Sūrah al-Tawbah exegesis on offensive warfare.
rows.anchor: only permission to defensive warfare is given here because until that time Muslims could not bear any burden beyond it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission rests both on the general right of self-defence and on Muslims having been targets of oppression, detailed in the next verse.
rows.anchor: every individual or group has the right to defend; moreover, Muslims have been a target of oppression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God can help Muslims defending themselves also warns Quraysh: though few, they are not helpless, and no force can defeat them once God helps.
rows.anchor: God is fully capable of helping them; once He starts helping them, no force in the world can defeat them

words: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description explains the oppression in the previous verse: Muslims were expelled without committing a crime, and the wording evokes the hardship of leaving one's homeland under compulsion.
rows.anchor: no one leaves his house and homeland unless he is utterly compelled

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is highly eloquent: the only alleged offence was declaring God their Lord, so their greatest virtue and truth was made their greatest sin.
rows.anchor: their greatest virtue and the greatest truth they preached became their greatest sin

rows.speaker: Some people
rows.claim: Some interpreters take the monotheistic declaration to mean that belief in one God is no offence and Quraysh harassed Muslims over an innocuous belief.
rows.anchor: Some people have interpreted this last sentence to refer to the fact that here the Qur’ān is presenting this declaration of monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the view that Quraysh dismissed monotheism as harmless: they understood its far-reaching implications and opposed the greatest truth, a folly the Qur'an subtly exposes.
rows.anchor: They knew its far reaching consequences and hence they were its enemies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ is the plural of ṣawmaʿah, used primarily for lofty structures where Christian monks lived in seclusion; monasteries is an apt translation.
rows.anchor: It is primarily used for the lofty mountains and buildings in which Christian monks would live in seclusion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biyaʿ is the plural of biʿah and denotes Jewish and Christian worship places; because ṣalawāt separately names Jewish prayer places, he takes biyaʿ here to mean Christian churches.
rows.anchor: this word must be considered specific to Christian places of worship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Churches and monasteries held equal importance for Christians because of their system of monasticism.
rows.anchor: both churches and monastries held equal importance to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt means places where Jews prayed; their word for prayer, ṣalwota, is Aramaic.
rows.anchor: which is an Aramaic word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid is the common word for Muslims' mosques.
rows.anchor: is commonly used for the mosques of Muslims

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God permits believers to fight even within the Ḥaram to defend themselves and protect religious values and symbols; prophets and messengers were likewise allowed jihad for this purpose, and Muslims received this permission to protect the Ḥaram.
rows.anchor: God has always allowed His prophets and messengers to wage jihād and they have waged it to protect their religious values and symbols

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the House's deceitful current custodians obstruct Muslims from defending it, Islahi says they should be repaid in kind.
rows.anchor: If its current deceitful and fraudulent claimants to custodianship imepede them in any way, they should be paid back in their own coin

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh accused Muslims of disregarding the Ḥaram's sanctity, joined in this campaign by Jews and Christians, who portrayed Muslim jihad as contrary to religious sentiment.
rows.anchor: The Jews and Christians too joined them in this vicious campaign and regarded the attitude of the Muslims to be against sentiments of religiosity

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an answers that if jihad for God meant violating religiosity, evil would have free rein to destroy religion itself.
rows.anchor: it would mean that evil is given full freedom to wreck havoc and obliterate religion itself

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christian monasteries and churches are named first because Christians were the strongest critics of Muslim jihad, with their concept of monasticism contributing greatly to their opposition.
rows.anchor: The reason for this foremost mention is that they it was they who were the most critical of the Muslim spirit of jihād

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call jihad irreligious should recognize that without it none of God's places of worship would have survived.
rows.anchor: if this concept pre-existed, none of God’s worship places on earth would have survived

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish and Christian worship places originally had the same standing as Muslim mosques; deviation arose when the People of the Book embraced polytheism and religious innovations.
rows.anchor: the worship places of the Jews and the Christians mentioned here primarily had the same status as mosques of the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of divine help is reiterated: those who protect God's symbols are helping their Lord, so God in turn will help them.
rows.anchor: those who strive to protect the symbols of God, in fact help their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people who fulfil their duty to the cause of truth merit God's help; He does not grant effortless comfort to those demanding it, as the Israelites did.
rows.anchor: He does not help those, who like the Israelites demand that God should provide them with a bed of roses without any effort from their own side

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful and needs no one's help; those who help Him are opening the way for His help to reach themselves.
rows.anchor: Since God is mighty and powerful, He does not need the help of anyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should not fear being few against many enemies, since the majestic God promising their help is powerful and dominant.
rows.anchor: Muslims should not feel scared because of their own small number and the large number of their enemies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers should not infer that a small Muslim group can achieve nothing: with God behind them, these drops will become a storm.
rows.anchor: These drops will now become a storm because God is behind them and God is mighty and powerful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land in verse 41 is Makkah, as in 13:41 and 21:44; local indications show that the permitted jihad concerns liberation of the Ḥaram.
rows.anchor: it refers to the land of Makkah because the jihād whose permission has been granted here primarily relates to the liberation of Ḥaram

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh had dishonoured Abraham's aims in settling his descendants in this land; if God grants authority to His servants, they will perform the stated duties, which were the reason God made this land a centre for Abraham and Ishmael.
rows.anchor: It was precisely these obligations for which God had made this land a place of centre for Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws)
